title: Colours and Colour Pickers
summary: ImGui works with colours in two forms - four floats from 0 to 1 (`ImVec4`) and one packed 32-bit integer (`ImU32`, built with `IM_COL32`). This lesson covers the colour widgets, converting between the forms and to HSV, and why packed colours store their bytes in the order they do.
markdown:
## Colour widgets

```cpp-norun
ImGui::ColorEdit3("Fog colour", &fog.color.x);        // float[3]: r, g, b from 0 to 1
ImGui::ColorEdit4("Tint", &sprite.tint.x);            // float[4]: with alpha
ImGui::ColorPicker4("Sky", &sky.x);                   // the big picker with a hue wheel or square
ImGui::ColorButton("##swatch", ImVec4(0.9f, 0.6f, 0.2f, 1.0f));   // a clickable swatch
```

`ColorEdit` shows the colour as numbers with a swatch; click the swatch for a picker popup. Flags choose the details: `ImGuiColorEditFlags_NoAlpha`, `DisplayHex`, `DisplayHSV`, `PickerHueWheel`, `Float` (0..1 numbers instead of 0..255), `HDR` (values above 1).

## Two forms of colour

**`ImVec4`**: four floats, red, green, blue, alpha, each from 0 to 1. Widgets and styles use this form.

**`ImU32`**: four bytes packed into one 32-bit unsigned integer. Draw lists use this form, because millions of vertices each carry a colour and four bytes are much smaller than four floats. The macro builds one:

```cpp-norun
ImU32 gold = IM_COL32(240, 180, 70, 255);    // r, g, b, a from 0 to 255
draw->AddRectFilled(min, max, gold);
```

With ImGui's default settings, `IM_COL32(r, g, b, a)` is

```
(a << 24) | (b << 16) | (g << 8) | r
```

Red is in the **lowest** byte. Written in memory on a little-endian PC (lesson 1.02 of the gamedev course), the bytes are in the order **R, G, B, A**, which is exactly the vertex format the GPU reads. That is why it looks "backwards" as a hexadecimal number: opaque red is `0xFF0000FF`.

Converting between them:

```cpp-norun
ImVec4 v = ImGui::ColorConvertU32ToFloat4(gold);
ImU32  u = ImGui::ColorConvertFloat4ToU32(ImVec4(1, 0.5f, 0, 1));   // rounds to the nearest of 0..255
ImU32  w = ImGui::GetColorU32(ImGuiCol_Text);                       // a style colour, with the current alpha
```

## HSV

Hue, saturation, value is a friendlier space for adjusting colours: change the hue to cycle through the rainbow while keeping brightness; lower the saturation to grey something out.

```cpp-norun
float h, s, v;
ImGui::ColorConvertRGBtoHSV(c.x, c.y, c.z, h, s, v);   // all in 0..1, hue too
h = std::fmod(h + 0.1f, 1.0f);                          // shift the hue
ImGui::ColorConvertHSVtoRGB(h, s, v, c.x, c.y, c.z);
```

A classic tool trick is to give each item a distinct colour from its index: hue = `i * 0.618034f` modulo 1 (the golden ratio spreads them evenly), saturation 0.6, value 0.9. The practice writes the conversions.

## Hexadecimal colour codes

Artists often paste colours as `#F0B446` or `#F0B446CC`. Parsing them into an `ImVec4` is a small, useful function, which the practice also has you write.

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] Building an ImU32 by hand in the wrong byte order
> `0xF0B446FF` is not gold with full alpha in ImGui's layout. Use IM_COL32 or ColorConvertFloat4ToU32.

> [!warning] Passing 0-255 values to ColorEdit
> ColorEdit edits floats from 0 to 1. Convert when your data stores bytes.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? What are ImGui's two forms of colour, and where is each used?
- ImVec4, four bytes 0..255, used by draw lists; ImU32, four floats 0..1, used by widgets
+ ImVec4, four floats 0..1, used by widgets and styles; ImU32, four packed bytes, used by draw lists
- ImVec4 for colours with alpha and ImU32 for colours without alpha, both used everywhere
> Widgets and styles edit ImVec4 floats; draw lists store a compact ImU32 per vertex. Both carry alpha.

? Why does IM_COL32 put red in the lowest byte?
- So that opaque red reads as 0xFF000000, the easiest form to type by hand
- Because the Windows API stores colours that way, and ImGui copies it
+ So that in memory on a little-endian machine the bytes are R, G, B, A, the vertex colour format the GPU reads
> The lowest byte comes first in memory on a little-endian PC. That is why the hexadecimal number looks backwards: opaque red is 0xFF0000FF.

? How do you give each of many items a distinct colour?
+ Spread hues by the golden ratio (i * 0.618 mod 1) at fixed saturation and value
- Add 10 to the red channel for each item, wrapping at 255
- Pick a random RGB colour for each item, a new one every frame
> Golden-ratio hues spread evenly however many items there are; convert each HSV colour to RGB. Random colours change every frame and can land close together.

? What does IM_COL32(255, 0, 0, 255) equal with ImGui's default byte order?
- 0xFFFF0000
+ 0xFF0000FF
- 0x00FF00FF
- 0xFF00FF00
> Alpha in the top byte, then blue, green, and red in the lowest byte.

? Why do draw lists use ImU32 instead of ImVec4?
- ImVec4 cannot hold an alpha value, only red, green and blue
+ Four bytes per vertex colour is far smaller than four floats
- The GPU cannot read floating-point colours from a vertex
> Every vertex carries a colour, so the saving adds up over millions of vertices.

? Which colour space makes "rotate through the rainbow at the same brightness" easy?
- RGB
- Packed ImU32
+ HSV
> In HSV you change only the hue and keep saturation and value.
```
